reading: FLOOR IS GONE in the 4-view bake: bottom-slab fraction 0.0564 (5.6%) vs 0.8728 (87.3%) single-view — the #267 floor reconstruction did NOT recur. The 4-view bake bottom-slab fraction (5.6%) is within 1pt of the parametric source's own (4.7%), which is the gauge/disc footprint geometry, not a floor.

AABB shape changed from [1.0, 0.3732, 1.0] (single-view: full-footprint flat slab) to [0.1819, 0.3655, 1.0] (4-view: thin in X, full depth in Z) — the flat full-width slab collapsed. Surface area dropped 6.3x (2.9385 -> 0.4649), consistent with the floor slab gone.
volumeRatio more than doubled (0.1323 -> 0.3427) and boundary edges dropped 3x (492156 -> 161367): the 4-view surface is more solid and less shredded.

CAVEAT (aspect ratio): both bakes read ~0.37 aspect (height / max(width,depth)) — the parametric source is 1.5833 (tall plate). The single-view aspect is saturated by the floor slab; the 4-view aspect is saturated by the depth axis (Z=1.0 normalized). Neither aspect ratio alone answers the identity question — the orchestrator grades the renders.

CAVEAT (rear axis splits): the 4-view z-axis farAreaFraction 0.5458 and fill fractions 0.91/0.98 are high because the object is now a THIN plate viewed along its depth (Z = normalized longest axis), NOT because the rear became fully informed — the pack has no back/top/bottom view and views carry no camera poses (#255 residual applies).
